text:
Ivy: Heads-up: onboarding reranker-v5 into staging; initial rankbench shows ndcg@10 down ~2.4% on recent-prod-corpus but mrr stable. Posting quick notes and checkpoints.
Marco: Interesting. Is this the new index pipeline with candidate merging?
Ivy: Yes — we've changed candidate indexing to incremental-merge (to reduce downtime). Index sizes per shard look fine but sample coverage seems off.
Selene: Can you share eval command and sample selection? We might be sampling a skewed cohort.
Ivy: rankbench --model reranker-v5 --candidates 300 --cohort recent-prod-corpus --sample 5000 --seed 11 --stratify time:7d
Marco: Stratify=time:7d could bias toward very recent docs where schema changed. Any document schema churn recently?
Ivy: Actually yes — last week we rolled new metadata field "summary_v2" and our indexer prefers summary_v2 over summary. Some older docs lack it.
Selene: That could change candidate scoring if model was fine-tuned using summary field heavily. Especially for short queries that match titles vs summaries.
Ivy: Breakdown: short queries ndcg@10 baseline 0.632 -> v5 0.605; long queries almost flat.
Marco: Seems summary_v2 present in ~38% of docs in sample. If indexer boosts docs with summary_v2, candidate pool composition changes. Any per-candidate-feature distribution?
Ivy: I pulled feature histograms: summary_v2_present: baseline 37.9% -> v5 sample 54.1% (index merge ordering pushed newer docs into top candidate windows).
Selene: So bias toward newer docs with summary_v2 could surface different negatives. Two paths: 1) normalize index scoring during bring-up (disable summary boost) 2) use stratified sampling in rankbench to match production candidate distribution.
Marco: Also check tokenization parity: indexer serialization clips to 1024 chars, reranker expects 1024 tokens. Could interact with summary_v2 length.
Ivy: Good catch. I verified serialization is char-based; will change to token-based truncation.
Selene: For eval comparability, let's also run a matched-sample test: create a sample where candidate distribution by "summary_v2_present" matches baseline distribution. That should separate model change vs index-composition effect.
Ivy: Running matched-sample A/B now (5000 queries).
ops-bot: "note: incremental-merge indexer rolled to staging at 2026-03-20T11:00:00Z"
Marco: Also, while you're running, include ndcg@1,@5,@10 and report top1 swap frequency per doc_age slice. That helps spot if recency boosting is moving top result.
Ivy: Will do. Early result (10% in): matched-sample ndcg@10 delta = -0.4% (within noise) vs full-sample -2.4%.
Selene: That strongly suggests index-composition caused most of the regression. Model itself likely ok.
Marco: Action items:
- Ivy: finish matched-sample A/B and post full stats; change serializer to token truncation.
- Selene: add rankbench stratifier option for arbitrary candidate-feature matching (owner: Selene).
- Marco: add a quick indexer sanity check to ops that warns when candidate-feature distribution deviates >5% from baseline.
ops-bot: "ticket: indexer-distribution-alert created (ops-1234)"
Ivy: Thanks. Will hold v5 rollout until we confirm no model-level regression. Ping here when A/B complete.
Selene: Nice find — indexer/composition issues are easy to misattribute to model changes. :eyes:
